draft.title: Hindu practice
card: Puja
Puja is worship offered to a deity, often through a murti (an image or statue). It can include prayers, flowers, light and food offerings.
Home and temple
Puja can take place at a home shrine or in a mandir (temple). Many Hindus worship at home daily, and may visit a temple on special occasions.
Festivals
Festivals mark events in Hindu stories and the seasons. Diwali, the festival of lights, is celebrated with lamps and family gatherings. Its stories vary between regions.
Pilgrimage
Pilgrimage is a journey to a sacred place, such as the river Ganges at Varanasi. Many Hindus travel to such places to worship and to seek spiritual benefit.
draft.remember: Hindu practice is expressed through puja, festivals and pilgrimage, in the home, the temple and sacred places.

a.q: Priya lights a lamp and offers flowers to a statue of a deity at a shrine in her kitchen. What is she doing?
opts: Performing puja at home
Going on a pilgrimage
Celebrating a festival at a temple
Studying a sacred text
a.why: Offering flowers and light to a deity's image is puja, and puja can be done at a home shrine. It is not a pilgrimage, because she has not travelled to a sacred place.
a.clue: Think about worship offered to a deity, and where she is.

b.q: Arjun travels from Sydney to Varanasi to bathe in the Ganges and pray. Which form of Hindu practice is this mainly?
opts: Pilgrimage to a sacred place
A festival held in the home
Daily puja at a home shrine
Worship held only in a temple
b.why: Travelling to a sacred place to worship and seek spiritual benefit is pilgrimage. He prays there, but the journey to a sacred place is the main feature, so it is not daily home puja.
b.clue: Focus on the journey to a sacred place.

problems.detail: The clue 'Focus on the journey to a sacred place' repeats the words of the right option 'Pilgrimage to a sacred place', so a student can match the clue to the option without knowing the idea.

The distractor 'Worship held only in a temple' uses 'only', while the card says puja 'can' take place at home or in a mandir. It is wrong as intended, but it breaks the rule against absolute words where the card uses 'can'.
